title: Increasing Wheat Plant Resilience to Climate Variability: The Role of Arbuscular Mycorrhizal Fungi in Adaptation to Drought Stress
content: Increasing climate variability and the growing frequency of extreme weather events pose serious challenges to agricultural productivity worldwide. Drought is among the most limiting abiotic stresses because it restricts nutrient uptake, reduces photosynthetic effi-ciency, and ultimately lowers crop yield. Arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi (AMF) form symbiotic associations with plant roots and can improve plant performance under wa-ter-deficit conditions. This proceeding paper examines the physiological and biochemical mechanisms through which AMF may enhance wheat tolerance to drought stress. Overall, AMF symbiosis was associated with greater chlorophyll retention, reduced accumulation of osmotic stress indicators, and higher antioxidant activity, suggesting improved cellular protection under drought. These observations highlight the potential value of AMF as a sustainable biological strategy for strengthening wheat resilience under climate variability.
